a.summary: The guard's failure output is two unordered ~30-element dumps of fully qualified class names with no diff, so it does not name the type it exists to catch.
a.failure_scenario: The exact scenario the guard is for -- a maintainer adds one record to the sealed hierarchy and forgets the fixture row -- fails with 'every concrete Token-2022 type needs a pinned Rust fixture and typed parser dispatch ==> expected: <[class software.sava.core.accounts.token.extensions.TokenGroupMember, class software.sava...., ...30 entries in HashSet iteration order...]> but was: <[...29 entries in a different order...]>'. JUnit 5's assertEquals(Object, Object, String) does no set diffing, so the maintainer must manually diff two ~1,900-character lines in arbitrary hash order to learn which class is missing a fixture -- information the test already has.

b.summary: The commit adds a new independent-oracle conformance assertion but reports no `Property/Oracle/Outcome` cluster, which AGENTS.md requires at handoff and which the predecessor commit in this same lineage supplied.
b.failure_scenario: The 25.11.0 handoff record contains no line stating what property the new `assertEquals(concreteTypes, fixtureTypes, ...)` walk pins or what oracle makes it independent of `Token2022.parseExtensions`. A later maintainer who finds this assertion failing after adding a `TokenExtension` subtype has no recorded statement that the fixture — not the Java dispatch — is the authority, and the cheapest way to make it pass is to add the type to the fixture side or to relax the assertion, which is exactly the 'passing assertion that merely locks in the bug' the rule exists to prevent. The owed line is roughly: Property: every concrete permitted subtype of the sealed TokenExtension hierarchy has typed dispatch in parseExtensions and exactly one pinned Rust fixture row, and no two Rust IDs collapse onto one Java type | Oracle: the committed upstream Rust fixture (29 rows) plus `TokenExtension.class.getPermittedSubclasses()`, neither derived from parseExtensions | Outcome: missing assertion added.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
